Mbabamwanawaresa (provisional designation ) is a mid-sized trans-Neptunian object in the classical Kuiper belt. It was discovered on March 11, 2005 by American astronomer Marc Buie at the Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona.
Names
The Minor Planet Center gave the object the provisional designation , which indicates its discovery date. The MPC later gave it the minor planet catalog number of 184314. The International Astronomical Union's Small Bodies Nomenclature Committee officially named the object Mbabamwanawaresa.
The name Mbabamwanawaresa is from the Zulu people of Southern Africa. In Zulu mythology, Mbaba Mwana Waresa is purportedly an agriculture, fertility, rain and harvest goddess who taught people how to make beer (umqombothi).
Orbit
Mbabamwanawaresa orbits the Sun at a distance of 38.8–51.1 AU once every ~300 years (semi-major axis of 45 AU). Its orbit has an eccentricity of 0.14 and an inclination of 6° with respect to the ecliptic.
